cases.ttl: Khushi Motors — four years of paid media across East Africa
cases.alt: Google Ads account overview: 1,238,753 clicks and the conversion-value trend
cases.body: Six advertising accounts across Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania and Pakistan, each run as its own island, none reconciled against what actually sold. I consolidated them into one reporting structure, rebuilt the campaign architecture around it, and moved budget by cost per released vehicle rather than cost per lead — the two disagree, and only one of them pays wages.

cases.ttl: An ROI dashboard built from nothing, reconciled to the cent
cases.body: Spend lived in the ad platforms, sales in a separate system, payments in spreadsheets. Nobody could answer what a sold vehicle had cost to sell. I built an entity-driven dashboard that pulls all three together, imported 402 months of spend across every branch and platform, and reconciled each payment to the cent — including currency conversion on locally invoiced ones.

cases.ttl: $25,968 of advertising that no report had ever counted
cases.body: One channel had run for five years and never appeared in a single report. The vehicles it sold were counted as though they had cost nothing. I found the spend in the archive, allocated it across branches by their share of its sales, spread package payments over the months they actually covered, and reconciled every payment at its implied exchange rate. It turned out to be the cheapest channel in the business, and it had been invisible.

cases.ttl: Arsh Premium Properties — Lahore real estate, two channels at once
cases.alt: Meta ad breakdown for a Lahore listing: impressions, spend, CPC and CTR per placement
cases.body: Premium apartments, penthouses and retail units priced in crores, listed on Zameen for intent and advertised on Meta for reach into Lahore, Karachi, Islamabad, Faisalabad and Sialkot. I built the strategy across both and tracked every property against its own spend rather than a pooled budget, so each listing could be judged on what it actually returned.

cases.ttl: Ocean Trading — hiring ads for a Japanese exporter
cases.body: Not selling anything — filling roles. Meta campaigns running alongside Indeed job listings, billed in yen, over three years. Recruitment advertising is judged on applications rather than leads, so the campaigns were built and read against clicks through to apply.

cases.alt: Search Console: 113k clicks and 6.1M impressions over twelve months against the prior period
cases.body: Paid media buys attention; search keeps it. Over twelve months the site went from 30.9k clicks to 113k, and from 1.09M impressions to 6.1M, against the same period a year earlier — average position improving from 10.4 to 6.9 as it went.
An audience built over years, gone overnight. I worked the recovery until the account was back under the company's control, then closed the hole that let it happen.

cases.ttl: A cloned website, traced and taken down
cases.body: Somebody stood up a near-identical copy of the company's site on a lookalike domain and ran it as their own. I traced it, documented the duplication, and pursued it until the copy came down.

cases.ttl: An email marketing platform built in-house instead of bought
cases.body: Rather than pay per contact per month to a vendor, the company got its own sending platform and an SEO content system beside it. Both built in-house, both owned outright, neither renewing.

cases.ttl: To Gear Marketing — twelve Canadian brands
cases.alt: Twelve client logos designed for a Canadian agency
cases.body: A Surrey agency's client roster, handled end to end: a daycare, construction and landscaping, a restaurant, a salon, plumbing, two pest control firms, limousine hire, glazing, property maintenance and a realtor. Logos, banners and service graphics for each, held to one standard so that a dozen small businesses looked like they could afford a design team.

cases.ttl: Five years of freelance work across ten websites
cases.body: Ten sites across AI tooling, crypto, legal technology and telecom — built, ranked, or both. Search strategy, technical fixes, content systems and the backlink work behind them.

figures: Of that, unrecorded until I found it
